questions.q: When uploading a customer list to create a Custom Audience:
options: Meta receives the emails in plain text in order to do the matching
The list travels hashed and matching never exposes data in the clear
First-party lists have been banned since iOS 14
It's only allowed with Reservation and signed consent
questions.explanation: Data is hashed BEFORE upload and matching happens on hashes: Meta never sees data in the clear. A legal basis for that use must also exist.

Which bid strategy is available for the category
The suitability of the content your ad appears next to
Which conversion events the dataset can receive
questions.explanation: The inventory filter governs adjacency: how strict you are about the content your ad shows up next to (expanded, moderate, limited).

questions.q: Trade-off of stricter brand safety controls:
options: More reach and lower cost thanks to better-quality adjacency
More brand protection but less reach and possibly higher cost
No effect on delivery, only on the report
They only apply to campaigns bought via Reservation
questions.explanation: Restricting inventory reduces available auctions: more safety, less reach, possibly higher cost. The planner balances it per client.

questions.q: An ad says: 'We know you have back problems; this is for you'. It's rejected because:
options: The health category is entirely banned on Meta
The Pixel isn't configured for that landing page
It uses Advantage+ placements in a sensitive category
It implies or asserts a personal attribute of the viewer
questions.explanation: Advertising Standards prohibit implying personal attributes (health, religion, finances...). Rephrase to a general product message.

questions.q: What does the ad review process check?
options: Only the final ad's image and video
Text, image, video, targeting and the destination landing page
Only the campaign budget and the chosen bid strategy
Only the campaign's objective and buying type
questions.explanation: Review evaluates the whole package against the Standards: creative, text, targeting and where you send people (the landing page).

questions.q: A client demands the strictest inventory filter + huge block lists. What do you warn?
options: Reach drops and cost may rise; protection must be balanced against efficiency
There's no effect on delivery as long as the creative is good quality
Meta forbids combining the strict filter with block lists
Block lists only work inside Audience Network
questions.explanation: Every restriction layer cuts available inventory. The right conversation is how much protection the brand needs vs how much cost it accepts.

questions.q: Which of these copies DOES comply with the Advertising Standards?
options: "We know you pay too much for electricity: this is for you"
"Lower your electricity bill with solar energy"
"For diabetics who can't stand their treatment anymore"
"Are you depressed? This supplement lifts you up"
questions.explanation: The general product message complies; the other three imply personal attributes of the viewer (finances, health, mental state).

questions.q: Legal basis for using a customer list in advertising:
options: The customer's consent/legal basis for that use of their data
It's enough that the email is corporate, not personal
It's only required if the list exceeds 10,000 records
Not applicable: hashing replaces the need for consent
questions.explanation: Hashing protects the transport, it doesn't legalize the use: you need the data subject's legal basis/consent. They're two different layers.

questions.q: A special ad category (housing, employment, credit) implies:
options: Targeting restrictions to prevent discrimination
Only a change in the auction's average CPM
Mandatory buying through Reservation at a fixed CPM
Uploading the customer list unhashed for auditing
questions.explanation: Special categories limit targeting options (age, gender, zones) to prevent discrimination in housing, employment and credit.

questions.q: Your ad was rejected and you believe it was a mistake. What do you do?
options: Request a review (appeal) from Account Quality
Duplicate the campaign until it passes the filter
Switch to another ad account and relaunch it
Edit only the ad set's name and republish
questions.explanation: The correct path is the appeal in Account Quality. Duplicating or gaming the review risks the entire account.
